newsitem.title: USA: Prom night turns tragic in New York.
newsitem.headline: Prom night turns tragic in New York.

text.p: The body of a young man who jumped from a cruise ship into the East River after a night of celebrating the senior prom was recovered by police Saturday.
Police originally said the drowning victim was a student at LaGuardia High School because the cruise had been rented to the school's senior class.

The school, formerly New York City High School for the Performing Arts, is a special school for musicians, artists and actors. The 1980 movie "Fame" and television series was based on the school programme.
"He is not a student at LaGuardia High School but was with a date from that school," said Carmen Melendez, a police spokeswoman.
A crewman from "The Spirit of New York" jumped into the murky water after the young man but could not find him. Witnesses reported hearing him call for help.
The drowning victim, believed to be in his 20s, has not been identified. The incident occurred shortly after 5 a.m. EDT at the South Street Seaport as the boat was docking at the pier.
His body was recovered at 2 p.m. EDT after an extensive search of the murky water by police scuba divers and Harbour Patrol.
The seaport, a popular tourist attraction, is in the Wall Street area of lower Manhattan.
